A Breath of Fresh Air: New Yachting Design House Kunsen Drops Its K37 Cabrio and Tender Concepts
17 photos
Photo: Kunsen Yachts
Sometimes, it takes years to get a project going, especially if you want it to actually break the limits of design. This is particularly true for the boating industry, one that has centuries of R&D already behind it. However, some teams manage to bring something fresh to the game.
That team is none other than Kunsen, a young boat design house that’s been around since 2022 but who have just begun to show their teeth. That’s four years of racking their brains to come up with two tenders that go well beyond what the average millionaire toy can achieve, and if I may, we’re in for a real treat.
Photo: Kunsen Yachts After diving into the project before us, I realized that the Kunsen K37 lineup really does have a solid chance of making it into the real world, with the project even going as far as seeing real scale models. Buckle up, because this one is going places.
Now, when creating the Kunsen K37, the very first project for Kunsen, the brand chose to use it to establish a “design language” for themselves. As we can see, the Kunsen defines itself with clean lines, clearly defined spaces, and a slightly purist Scandinavian look.
But, once we peek beyond the design, we realize what Kunsen has achieved here. One of the initial tricks of the first K37 designs included the ability to hide the rear-facing lounge in the belly of the tender through a network of hydraulics that lowered or raised this feature into place.
Photo: Kunsen Yachts If it’s visible, we unlock the sun beds we see. If it’s hidden under the floor however, the K37 created a ground-level lounge while leaving the rear free of any obstructions, perfect for when you’re in some bay and decide to go for a swim.
A neat trick, to say the least and one that was ultimately ditched, and it’s easy to understand why; to make it work, entire new systems would need to be integrated into the tenders, not to mention pushing the boat to the brink of its weight limits or the production nightmares that may arise.
As the model progressed, Kunsen ultimately decided to craft two versions: the Cabrio and the Tender. The Cabrio is the one with the exposed rear sun bed, while the Tender places the lounge into the floor of the main deck.
Kunsen didn’t stop there, accompanying each of the designs with two bulwark terraces or balconies slash diving platforms. These not only expand the deck space, but also extend lounging options over open waters. Imagine hanging your feet off this ledge, taking a sip of champagne, and just taking it all in; there are no sharks in this daydream.
Photo: Kunsen Yachts Yet, we’re still not done with lounging options, with another sun bed visible at the bow of the boats and accessible by a walkway that runs along both sides of the wheelhouses. A teak deck balances the dark tones of the design but also stays as cool as possible while baking under constant exposure to the sun.
Be it the Tender or the Cabrio, both offer overnight and enclosed accommodations to their owners. The head, located in the lower level and at the front of the ship, places quite the amount of features at our disposal.
At the very tip of a 37, a large triangular bed is in place, and judging by the pads that make it up, it may be modular, capable of transforming into a U-shaped lounge when desired. Considering there’s a little wine bar and galley nearby, it would make a whole lot of sense.
Photo: Kunsen Yachts This kitchen is located on the starboard side of the ship, and port, the entrance to the head is occupied by a bathroom with toilet, shower, sink, and storage for essentials. This is the sort of bathroom you don’t often find in tenders such as these.
Since this team has plans to make these tenders a real product, they have also thought of the propulsion of the K37 class and worked out the placement of batteries, wiring, thrusters, engines, and inverters. It’s a hybrid setup that calls upon a mix of electric and combustion power to get moving. Dimensions are also complete; obviously, since there a scale model in the real world.
Photo: Kunsen Yachts That said, does the boating industry have a place for the K37 Tender and Cabrio? Personally, I’d say yes, but with a bit of a reservation based on the fact that these babies are pretty big, rolling in with a total length of 39,86 ft (12.15 m), so there needs to be an equally grand garage and those are typically found in superyachts.
Maybe Kunsen chooses to market these babies to coastline and island-hopping millionaires around the world as boats to be used as day boats, one with the ability to keep us under the stars too once we find some hidden cove somewhere.
Currently, Kunsen does have an “inquire” tab available on their website, so plans to make these babies a real deal is clearly much closer than we think.
